title: We have made the alert fast and left the recovery exactly as slow as it ever was
explanation: Three disasters on three continents in one weekend, and all three have the same shape: the detection system did its job in hours and then handed off to nothing. A tsunami warning is issued and lifted the same morning; a flash flood emergency expires; a fire is contained overnight. Each of those is a measured, quantitative, minutes-to-hours system. What follows - the death toll, the grid, the intensive care unit, the people who will not go back into the house - has no equivalent instrument and no equivalent urgency. The alert clearing has become the moment coverage ends, which is roughly the moment the actual damage begins to be counted.

evidence.text: Moke has now fully dissipated - the storm itself is gone, its circulation opened into a trough. That's the fast instrument closing the file. Nothing closes the file on what Lala's saturated ground still owes the Big Island, or on how many named systems it will take before that debt is actually paid down.

The tsunami warning resolved in one morning, nine days ago. The country's top leadership only just caught up to the ground: VP Gibran toured East Nusa Tenggara on Aug 20, President Prabowo reached Nagekeo on Aug 26. The instrument that measures political attention arriving runs even slower than the one counting the dead.

NIPSCO hit ~99% restoration by its own deadline - genuinely fast, as these things go. But the company's own footnote is the point: some individual properties will take longer, with no instrument tracking which ones or for how long. A 99% headline and a 0% headline look identical to whoever's still in the dark.

retired_reason: All three feeder storylines resolved and rolled off the cabinet during the weekly rollover (Moke dissipated and went dormant, Indiana's outage reached full restoration, Indonesia's recovery is proceeding without new developments) - no fresh accumulation for two consecutive cycles. Retiring at the natural checkpoint of the week's rollover rather than letting it sit stale into the new week.
